How Much Does It Cost to Paint a House in Sydney?

Posted on 31 Aug at 9:00 am

If you're planning to repaint your home, the first question is almost always the same: what will it actually cost? The honest answer is that it depends on the scope, because no two homes are identical. This guide from Sydney Paintmasters, a licensed team offering professional house painting in Sydney, breaks down the real cost factors so you can set a realistic budget and compare quotes fairly. We won't pretend there's a single magic number, but by the end you'll understand what drives the price, roughly what to expect and how to make sure the quotes you receive are comparing like with like.

Quick answer

In Sydney, house painting typically costs about $15 to $45 per square metre, or roughly $3,500 to $12,000 or more for a standard home, depending on interior vs exterior, surface condition, number of coats, access and prep. Careful surface preparation is the biggest driver of both price and how long the finish lasts.

What affects the cost of painting a house in Sydney?

Several things combine to determine what a repaint costs, and understanding them helps you see why quotes can vary so much between jobs. The main factors are:

  • Size and square metres: the more wall and ceiling area to cover, the more paint and labour required, which is the single biggest driver of the total.
  • Interior vs exterior: exterior work often costs more because of weather preparation, height and the more durable coatings involved.
  • Surface condition and preparation: sound walls need less work than surfaces with cracks, flaking paint, water damage or mould to repair first.
  • Number of coats: bare surfaces, big colour changes and dark-to-light changes may need extra coats, which adds time and materials.
  • Paint quality: premium paints cost more up front but tend to cover better and last longer.
  • Access and height: multi-storey homes, steep sites and hard-to-reach areas may need scaffolding or special access, which adds to the price.
  • Detail work: trims, ceilings, doors, feature walls and intricate cutting-in all take extra time.

Because these vary from home to home, the only way to get an exact figure is a proper look at your property. What the factors above give you is a clear sense of why the number moves and where your money goes.

Why surface preparation drives the price

If there's one factor worth understanding, it's preparation. Good prep, washing, filling, sanding, repairs and priming, is where a quality, long-lasting finish comes from, and it's often the most time-consuming part of the job. It's also exactly where a suspiciously cheap quote usually cuts corners. Skipping prep gets a painter on and off site faster and lowers the price, but the paint fails sooner, so you pay again far too soon. When you compare quotes, the prep is where the real difference in value hides.

Typical house painting price ranges in Sydney

To help you budget, here are indicative ranges for Sydney. Treat these as a general guide to set expectations, not as fixed prices, because your actual cost depends on the factors above:

ScopeTypical Sydney range (guide only)
Interior repaint (walls, ceilings and trims)around $3,500 to $8,000 for a standard home
Exterior repaintaround $4,000 to $10,000 or more, higher for large or multi-storey homes
Full interior and exterior repaintaround $8,000 to $15,000 or more for a standard home
Per square metre guidearound $15 to $45 per m2 depending on prep and coats

Typical Sydney market ranges only, not a quote. Every job is priced on site.

These are typical Sydney market ranges, not a quote from Sydney Paintmasters. A small, sound home in good condition sits at the lower end, while a large home needing significant repairs and prep sits higher. The accurate number always comes from an on-site assessment of your home.

Interior vs exterior painting costs

One of the biggest reasons quotes differ is whether you're painting inside, outside or both. Interior painting is generally more straightforward: the surfaces are protected from the weather, access is usually easier and the main work is careful preparation, cutting-in and a clean finish around fixtures and trims. Exterior painting tends to cost more, and for good reason. Exterior surfaces face Sydney's sun, rain, salt and temperature swings, so they need more thorough weather preparation and more durable, weather-resistant coatings that stand up to the conditions. Height and access add to it too, since upper storeys, eaves, gutters and steep or awkward areas may require scaffolding or special equipment to reach safely. The exterior of your home is also its first line of defence against the elements, so the coatings used are built to protect as much as to beautify. When you understand this, the price difference between interior and exterior work makes sense: you're not just paying for more paint, you're paying for the extra preparation, protection and access that outdoor surfaces demand.

How to compare painting quotes without getting burned

Comparing painting quotes on price alone is how people end up disappointed, because the cheapest quote often leaves out the very things that make a paint job last. A good, honest quote should itemise what you're actually getting. Look for a clear description of the preparation work included, since this is where quality and durability come from and where cheap quotes cut corners. Check the number of coats being applied, as two proper coats will outperform one thin one. See what products are specified, because quality paints perform better and last longer. Ask whether any warranty or guarantee on workmanship is offered, and importantly, confirm the painter is licensed. In New South Wales, painting work over a certain value must be done by a licensed tradesperson, so checking a painter holds a current licence protects you and is a basic mark of a legitimate operator. A quote that spells out prep, coats, products and licensing lets you compare like with like. One that's simply a single low number with no detail is the one to be wary of, because you can't see what's been left out.

How to get an accurate quote for your home

Ultimately, the only way to know exactly what your repaint will cost is a proper, on-site quote, and it's worth getting one rather than relying on rough estimates. During a free on-site quote, a painter can see your home in person: the true size and condition of the surfaces, the amount of preparation and repair needed, access and height considerations, and the specific scope you want, whether that's walls only, a full interior, the exterior or the whole home. That's what allows an accurate, fixed price rather than a guess, and it also gives you the chance to discuss colours, finishes and timing, and to ask the questions that help you feel confident about who you're hiring. A good painter will happily walk you through what's included and why. The assessment costs you nothing, and it turns the general ranges in this guide into a real number for your home, so you can budget with certainty and move ahead knowing exactly what you're getting.

Frequently asked questions

What is the average cost to paint a 3-bedroom house in Sydney?

There's no single average, because it depends on interior versus exterior, the condition of the surfaces and how much prep is needed. As a rough guide, a standard home repaint often falls somewhere between $3,500 and $12,000 or more. The accurate figure for your home comes from a free on-site quote.

Is it cheaper to paint the interior or exterior of a house?

Interior painting is usually cheaper per job, because exterior work involves more weather preparation, more durable coatings and often height and access challenges like scaffolding. Exterior surfaces have to withstand sun, rain and salt, so they cost more to prepare and coat properly. The gap varies with your home's size and condition.

How long does it take to paint a house in Sydney?

It depends on the size of the home, the scope and how much preparation is required, so timeframes vary widely from a few days to a couple of weeks. Weather can also affect exterior work. Your painter can give you a realistic schedule once they've assessed your home during the quote.

Does cheaper paint cost more in the long run?

Often, yes. Cheaper paint and, more importantly, skipped preparation tend to fail sooner, so you repaint again far too soon and pay twice. Quality paint applied over thorough prep costs more up front but lasts longer, which usually works out more economical over the life of the finish. Prep is the real difference.

Do I need a licensed painter in NSW?

In New South Wales, painting work above a certain value must be carried out by a licensed tradesperson. Using a licensed painter protects you and is a basic sign of a legitimate, accountable operator. It's always worth confirming a painter holds a current licence before you hire. Sydney Paintmasters holds Licence 315254C.

Final thoughts

Painting a house in Sydney isn't a one-price job, because the cost depends on scope, surface condition, prep, coats and access, but understanding those factors lets you budget realistically and compare quotes with confidence. The biggest lesson is that thorough preparation, not the cheapest quote, is what makes a paint job look good and last. Backed by 20+ years of experience and Licence 315254C, we're happy to give you an honest, fixed price on your house painting project in Sydney.
